summary: Bethany-style 54-foot fire tower in Sumter National Forest, Oconee County, SC, dated around 1935; Forest Service still uses it on emergency fire-danger days; NHLR-registered 2013.

facts.design: 54-foot Bethany tower, similar to an Aermotor, with 7x7 metal cab and low hip roof

access.note: Still used by the Forest Service on emergency fire-danger days; the register gives no public climbing rules.

events.note: Newspaper reports plans for a fire watch tower on Long Nose mountain, west of Walhalla; not clearly this site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Long Mountain Tower (US 961, SC 15) is a separate register entry in the same ranger district, with a similar 1935 date and a different tower model. Its history is not applied to this tower.

notes_for_editor: Brief lacked design and height; added from NHLR (54 ft = 16.5 m). Brief elevation 645.3 m matches NHLR 645 m. OpenStreetMap node 357111624 tags ele=658, not used. Build date is unresolved: NHLR says around 1935, but a February 1941 newspaper item, as reprinted by Forest Lookouts, announces plans for a tower on Long Nose mountain west of Walhalla. The story gives both; this may be a replacement or a different site. Current use is undated (NHLR). No source read documents public access or current condition. Search results for Long Mountain (a Facebook reel and a blog) were not read as page text and are not used. No photos. Confidence is low because the only substantive source is the register.
